topics.definition: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes and contains one or more containers.
tips: Usually run one main application per Pod.

topics.definition: Pods move through phases such as Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed and Unknown.
tips: Use kubectl get pods to check status.

topics.definition: Labels organize resources and selectors identify matching resources.
A Service provides stable network access to one or more Pods.
tips: Services use labels to find Pods.

topics.definition: Default Service type that exposes an application inside the cluster.
tips: Not accessible from outside the cluster.

topics.definition: Exposes a Service on a static port of every worker node.
topics.example: Access web app via node IP

topics.definition: Creates an external load balancer to expose a Service.
Use labels consistently, keep Pods lightweight and expose only required services.
